subject: HealthScout order form — inspection protocol, pen-test window & evidence cadence
messages:
From: Caroline Myers <cmyers@healthscout.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T09:12:00Z
Subject: HealthScout order form — inspection protocol & pen test window

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for sending over the draft order form earlier this week. Legal Ops ran a quick review and flagged two items we need to lock down before we can route the MSA to procurement: the inspection/audit rights language in the security exhibit and the pen-test access window.

Primary asks:
- Can Redwood confirm the proposed pen-test window (we prefer Oct 18–22 or Nov 1–5)?
- We need a clear evidence cadence for SOC 2 artifacts and a contact list for evidence requests (who to ping and SLA for responses).
- Slight redline request: limit on-demand forensic access to a scoped sampling (not full tenant extraction) — we can share suggested wording.

Attaching a short checklist of our expectations for scope and evidence cadence. Can you confirm an internal owner and a point of contact for the security exhibit review?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement needs this by next Friday.

Best,
Caroline
Caroline Myers
Director, Security & Compliance
HealthScout Inc.

Attachments: HealthScout_Audit_Checklist.pdf (attached)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Myers <cmyers@healthscout.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: HealthScout order form — inspection protocol & pen test window

Caroline — thanks for the clear asks. Laura and I reviewed the checklist; Neha from legal is copied for clause guidance. High-level answers below and next steps at the bottom.

Pen-test window: We can commit to a scoped pen-test window in both Oct and Nov as backups. Proposed primary window: Oct 18–22, fallback Nov 1–5. We will require a 10-business-day notice to schedule staging access, and a 48-hour blackout for production traffic changes.

Audit/inspection rights: Redwood is willing to accept a bounded inspection carve-out in the security exhibit. Proposed limits:
- Tenant-scoped forensic access only; no raw backups/stream exports.
- Sampling bands (up to 3% of production samples) and mutually agreed selectors.
- Written notice + on-site/remote modality options; request-response SLA: 5 business days for evidence requests.

SOC 2 artifacts & cadence: Suggested cadence for evidence handover:
- Quarterly automated report deliveries (system logs summary + control attestation).
- One-off evidence pulls within 5 business days for urgent requests (flagged in the Cc to compliance@redwood.com).

Attachments I’m sending: HealthScout_PenTest_Scope_v1.pdf (scope template), HealthScout_Evidence_Matrix.xlsx (proposed cadence). Please review and let us know which items in the matrix are must-haves vs. nice-to-have.

Next steps / owners:
- Laura Bennett (security eng) — will take the lead on technical evidence mapping and confirm what we can provide by quarter vs ad-hoc.
- Neha Kapoor (legal) — will propose specific redline language for the MSA security exhibit and for the pen-test clause.
- I’ll confirm the pen-test calendar once you pick primary/fallback dates.

If that works, Neha will circulate redline suggestions by EOD tomorrow and Laura will send the initial evidence mapping by Friday.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: HealthScout_PenTest_Scope_v1.pdf, HealthScout_Evidence_Matrix.xlsx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Myers <cmyers@healthscout.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: HealthScout order form — inspection protocol & pen test window

Caroline / team — looping in formal redlines and rationale below. I’ve attached an annotated MSA excerpt (MSA_redlines_annotated.docx) with tracked changes; highlights: 

1) Audit rights (Section 7.3): replace broad "full access" phrasing with "tenant-scoped, for-cause and scheduled inspections limited to relevant business processes and logs." This preserves the customer’s right while protecting PII and platform integrity.

2) Pen test clause: we propose a scoped pen-test clause allowing third-party tests against staging and agreed selectors in production under strict rules:
   - 10-business-day notice, signed testing plan, and a mutually approved tester.
   - No exploitation of customer data; all findings delivered to both parties and high/critical items triaged within 3 business days.

3) Evidence cadence: set a baseline of quarterly artifact drops and an expedited 5-business-day SLA for ad-hoc requests. We can include a separate "evidence appendix" that lists controls we can provide and the delivery modality (CSV, filtered logs, screenshots).

I’m happy to walk through the redlines on a quick call if that helps procurement move faster.

Neha Kapoor
Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: MSA_redlines_annotated.docx

From: Caroline Myers <cmyers@healthscout.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@healthscout.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T16:34:00Z
Subject: Re: HealthScout order form — inspection protocol & pen test window

Dylan / Neha — this looks great, thank you. HealthScout can accept the tenant-scoped language and the pen-test governance you proposed. A couple quick notes: 

- We prefer the Oct 18–22 window (primary). Please lock resources and confirm the approved staging IP range by Oct 1.
- For the evidence matrix, we’ll mark the following as must-haves: SOC 2 system descriptions, user access change logs (90 days), and a sample of request-response latency logs. Everything else is negotiable.
- Procurement will prepare a short addendum to the order form referencing the evidence appendix. I’ll share the procurement tracker and DocuSign link once Laura confirms the final wording.

Action items:
- Dylan: confirm staging access checklist and point Laura to the vendor white-list for IPs.
- Laura: populate the evidence mapping with expected export formats.
- Neha: finalize the annotated redlines and confirm we’re aligned on the 5-business-day SLA.

We’ll plan for a 30-minute sync on Oct 4 if that suits you — Caroline, Laura and I will be on that call.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

Best,
Caroline
Caroline Myers
Director, Security & Compliance
HealthScout Inc.
